description:
Decide whether `jit claim acquire` and `jit issue claim` append `IssueClaimed` from the issue record's assignee alone, so a claim parses no event-log record and writes its event exactly when the assignment changes.

## Background

`jit claim acquire` synchronizes the issue through `MutationIntent::ClaimIssue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs`). Its capture requests the whole event log. The finalizer parses it (`captured_events`, `repository_state/mutation.rs`) and asks whether the log's tail already shows this claim (`event_tail_reflects_claim`). So after acquire and `issue unassign`, a second acquire writes the issue with no event, against @/inv/event-log, and an issue assigned outside jit with no claim event gets a repair event. Every event append already reads only the log's bounded end (`CaptureSpec::discover_tail`, `repository_state/image.rs`), and the issue write and its events publish in one redo record. The doc comments on the claim capture in `commands/claim.rs` describe the whole-log read.

`jit issue claim` (lifecycle `Claim`, `commands/mod.rs`) pushes `IssueClaimed` unconditionally, including when a Ready issue already assigned to the claimant is promoted. `issue assign` emits it only when the assignee changes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `claim acquire` captures the issue record and the log's tail only. It appends `IssueClaimed` exactly when the captured issue's assignee differs from the claimant, in the same redo record as the issue write, and appends nothing otherwise.
- [hard] REQ-02: `captured_events` and `event_tail_reflects_claim` no longer exist, the claim decision reads no event-log record, and the doc comments on the claim capture match.
- [hard] REQ-03: Tests show that acquire, unassign, acquire appends two claim events; that a repeated claim appends nothing; and that a claim of an issue already assigned to the claimant outside jit appends nothing.
- [hard] REQ-04: `issue claim` appends `IssueClaimed` exactly when the assignee changes; a same-assignee promotion appends only the state change, and a test pins it.

## Notes

- A claim does not repair a missing claim event for an assignment made outside jit.
- `claim acquire` overwriting another assignee with no refusal or release event is existing behaviour and out of scope.
title: Claim acquire emits its event exactly when the assignee changes
